newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAGACH LOSES GOLD MEDAL FOR DOPING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAGACH LOSES GOLD MEDAL FOR DOPING.

text.p: World shot champion Aleksandr Bagach was stripped of his gold medal on Thursday and lost $60,000 prize money after testing positive for the stimulant ephedrine.
The 30-year-old Ukrainian, who became on Saturday the first person to win a title at the sixth world championships, also became the first athlete to fail a drug test here.
American John Godina, competing here after he was granted a wild card as defending champion, is the new world shot champion while German Oliver-Sven Buder has the silver.
C.J. Hunter, fiancee of the new women's 100 metres champion Marion Jones, is elevated to the bronze medal position.
French men's 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan also tested positive for ephedrine. Their results were also cancelled.
All three are beneficiaries of the International Amateur Athletic Federation's decision to scrap bans for first offenders for minor drugs such as stimulants and replace them with a "public warning".
Bagach has already tested positive once during his career, failing a test for testosterone at the 1989 European Cup in Gateshead, England, while competing for the Soviet Union.
The first gold medal of the sixth day of the championships went to Poland's Robert Korzeniowski who triumphed in the 50 kms walk despite the fierce morning heat.
Korzeniowski moved to northern France to train because the conditions were similar to his native country but showed on Thursday he can master any conditions.

"It's really weird," Korzeniowksi said. "I don't like the heat and I don't train in hot conditions but I concentrated well and I'm starting to get used to it now that nearly every championship is held in the heat."
The Olympic champion strode away from the pack with 1997 World Cup winner Jesus Garcia of Spain after 34 kms. The pair duelled for a further 10 kms before Korzeniowski made his decisive break.
Former world women's long jump champions Heike Drechsler and Jackie Joyner-Kersee both qualified for Saturday's final along with Jones, who won the women's 100 final on Sunday.
Briton Tessa Sanderson, 41, the oldest woman to take part at a world championships, was eliminated in the qualifying stages of the javelin and will not be seen on the international stage again.
"There was a tear in my eye as I stood on the runup, knowing this was my last ever throw," said the 1984 Olympic champion.
